patients.label: 19-year-old female cheerleader with simultaneous bilateral patella tendon rupture after a trampoline injury

identity_evidence.quote: Our patient is a 19-year-old Chinese female who is an active cheerleader.

attribution_limitations: MRI wording places the complete rupture in the bilateral proximal patellar tendons, while the intra-operative description places the left-knee rupture in the mid-portion of the patella tendon.
The sentence calling the tendon thin and narrow says it may have contributed to the injury; causation is not established.
The source does not say when gait retraining and strengthening progressed.

claims.text: A 19-year-old Chinese female active cheerleader somersaulted in mid-air on a trampoline, landed on her feet with her knees slightly flexed and felt immediate excruciating pain. She could not stand independently and was brought to the emergency department by ambulance, then admitted. She had no past medical history, no family history of connective tissue disorders, and no previous prolonged antibiotic or steroid usage.

claims.text: Postoperatively she wore bilateral knee braces locked in extension for 2 weeks, was reviewed every 2 weeks up to 2 months with progressive flexion, and had physiotherapy up to a year. She reached 0° to 100° at 3 months and the braces were removed, walked without a limp at 5 months, and had 0° to 130° with restored quadriceps bulk at 12 months. At last review 2.5 years after surgery she had excellent outcomes and had returned to hiking and jogging.
